title: Delinquency and Credit Reporting Thresholds for Credit Builder Accounts
content:
Every Credit Builder Accounts plan is reported to Equifax, Experian and TransUnion every month. A missed payment is reported to the credit bureaus once it reaches the reporting threshold, and the account is closed for delinquency at the closing threshold.

| Plan | Bureaus reported every month | Days past due at which a missed payment is reported | Days past due at which the account is closed for delinquency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credit Builder 600 Plan | Equifax, Experian, TransUnion | 30 | 60 |
| Credit Builder 1000 Plan | Equifax, Experian, TransUnion | 30 | 60 |
| Credit Builder 1200 Plan | Equifax, Experian, TransUnion | 30 | 90 |
| Credit Builder 1800 Plan | Equifax, Experian, TransUnion | 30 | 90 |
| Credit Builder 2400 Plan | Equifax, Experian, TransUnion | 30 | 90 |
| Credit Builder 3000 Plan | Equifax, Experian, TransUnion | 30 | 90 |

The two 12-month plans (Credit Builder 600 Plan and Credit Builder 1000 Plan) close for delinquency at 60 days past due; the four longer plans at 90 days past due. The reporting threshold is 30 days past due on all six.
